query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of yttrium oxide to a magnesium-based alloy can enhance its glass-forming ability.
generation.conditions: Rapid solidification at a cooling rate of 10^5 K/s
generation.mechanism: Heterogeneous nucleation inhibition and increased atomic packing density
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in the glass-forming ability, measured by the critical cooling rate, relative to the baseline alloy without yttrium oxide addition
generation.baseline: Magnesium-based alloy without yttrium oxide addition
generation.boundary: The critical cooling rate for glass formation
generation.uncertainty: The optimal concentration of yttrium oxide and the cooling rate may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of magnesium-based alloys with varying concentrations of yttrium oxide, and measure their glass-forming ability using differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured critical cooling rate is not increased by at least 15% relative to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
